_description: Autonomous performance agent working memory. Read and written by perf-agent on every cycle. Do not edit manually — the agent owns this file.
_instructions: See .github/perf-agent-prompt.md for the algorithm that operates on this file.

north_star.description: 90% of MongoDB Community throughput across all YCSB workloads

stuck_detection.comment: If average ratio improves by less than 2pp over the last 3 benchmark cycles, the plan is stuck.

current_plan.name: Plan V3: Profile-First Performance Recovery
current_plan.rationale: A week of static-analysis-driven optimization produced no measurable throughput improvement. The benchmarks measured CI noise, not real performance. The highest-leverage missing pieces are: (1) runtime profiling to identify actual bottlenecks, (2) per-message bufio allocation fix, (3) bbolt.Batch() for write coalescing. All prior optimization was guesswork without a flame graph.
current_plan.architectural_ceiling: bbolt is a single-writer B-tree. Realistic ceiling with all fixes applied: 50-70% of MongoDB on reads, 30-50% on writes with syncOnWrite=true. If benchmark ratio plateaus below 60% after Phase 2 completes, the strategic question is whether to accept the bbolt ceiling or migrate to Pebble (LSM, Apache 2.0, concurrent writers).

phases.name: Instrumentation — Profile Before Touching Anything
phases.rationale: Cannot sequence Phase 1 fixes correctly without flame graph data. P0-B (bufio) is the single highest-ROI change in the codebase and has zero risk.

items.name: Add pprof endpoint to admin HTTP server
items.description: Register net/http/pprof routes on the admin mux at :27080. Import _ 'net/http/pprof' and add HandleFunc registrations for /debug/pprof/, /debug/pprof/profile, /debug/pprof/trace, /debug/pprof/symbol. This enables CPU profiling, heap profiling, goroutine traces, and allocation profiling without code changes to collect.
items.success_criteria: curl http://localhost:27080/debug/pprof/ returns the pprof index page listing available profiles.

items.name: Fix per-message bufio.Reader allocation
items.description: ReadMessage() at internal/wire/protocol.go calls bufio.NewReaderSize(lr, 4096) on every single message — one 4KiB allocation per request on the hottest path. Fix: move *bufio.Reader to the Connection struct, initialize once in newConnection with bufio.NewReaderSize(conn, 16*1024), pass c.br to ReadMessage instead of c.conn. Change ReadMessage signature to accept io.Reader instead of net.Conn. Remove the internal bufio.NewReaderSize call from ReadMessage. Add a matching *bufio.Writer to Connection for response buffering, initialized as bufio.NewWriterSize(conn, 32*1024), flush at end of each handleMessage call.
items.success_criteria: go test ./internal/wire/... passes. BenchmarkReadMessage shows zero bufio.NewReader allocations per operation.

items.name: Set TCP_NODELAY on accepted connections
items.description: After listener.Accept(), cast conn to *net.TCPConn and call SetNoDelay(true) and SetKeepAlive(true). Without TCP_NODELAY, Nagle's algorithm buffers small responses until 40ms timeout fires, adding systematic tail latency.
items.success_criteria: All existing tests pass. ss -tnp | grep 27017 shows NODELAY on connections.

items.name: Set GOMEMLIMIT in bench docker-compose
items.description: Add GOMEMLIMIT=512MiB to the Salvobase container environment in the bench docker-compose. Do NOT set GOGC above 100 — higher GOGC is wrong for write-heavy servers (larger heap = longer GC pauses when GC fires). GOMEMLIMIT alone bounds heap growth while keeping GC responsive.
items.success_criteria: docker-compose.yml shows GOMEMLIMIT env var. No change to GOGC default.

items.name: Add per-layer latency histograms
items.description: Add Prometheus histograms breaking down request latency into 4 layers: (1) salvo_wire_parse_seconds — OP_MSG parse time, (2) salvo_bson_process_seconds — extractAndStripMeta + injectField time, (3) salvo_storage_seconds — bbolt transaction time, (4) salvo_response_write_seconds — write response to conn. Use ExponentialBuckets(0.00001, 2, 15) for wire/bson/response and ExponentialBuckets(0.0001, 2, 12) for storage. These histograms let you see where time goes without running a profiler.
items.success_criteria: curl /metrics after a 60-second YCSB run shows all 4 histogram families with non-zero bucket counts.

phases.name: Fix the Top Bottlenecks
phases.gate_description: All Phase 0 items must be merged before Phase 1 begins. The flame graph should be captured manually or via a CI step to confirm bottleneck ordering, but P1-A and P1-B are high-confidence regardless.
phases.rationale: These three fixes address the most likely bottlenecks based on code analysis and architectural constraints. The fsync-per-write issue is the proven killer for write workloads. The BSON allocation pooling addresses GC pressure on all workloads. Both are low-risk changes.

items.name: Pool BSON scratch buffers with sync.Pool
items.description: extractAndStripMeta() and injectField() do full BSON unmarshal→rebuild→remarshal on every request. Add sync.Pool for: (1) bson.D slices (pool with capacity 16), (2) marshal output byte buffers (pool *bytes.Buffer, reset between uses), (3) index key construction buffers in internal/storage/index.go. This does not eliminate copies but eliminates GC churn. Replace make([]byte, ...) in these hot paths with pool get/put pairs.
items.success_criteria: BenchmarkInsertMany -benchmem shows 2-4 fewer allocations per operation. go test ./... passes.

items.name: Use bbolt.Batch() for concurrent unordered writes
items.description: bbolt allows one writer at a time. Under 16 YCSB threads, all write goroutines serialize behind boltDB.Update(). bbolt has a built-in batch API (db.Batch()) that coalesces concurrent calls automatically. CRITICAL: bbolt.Batch() retries individual transactions on conflict — closures MUST reset all mutable state at the top (ids = ids[:0], successCount = 0, insertErr = nil) or retries use stale values. Only use Batch() for opts.Ordered == false inserts; keep Update() for ordered inserts where error semantics matter. After bolt.Open, set: db.MaxBatchSize = 500, db.MaxBatchDelay = 5 * time.Millisecond. This turns N serial fsyncs into 1 fsync per batch window under concurrent load.
items.success_criteria: BenchmarkInsertMany with 16 goroutines shows throughput increase. All ordered-insert duplicate-key tests still pass. go test ./... passes.

items.name: Pass --syncOnWrite=false in bench docker-compose
items.description: The bench docker-compose does not pass --syncOnWrite=false to Salvobase. The default syncOnWrite=true means every boltDB.Update() fsyncs — killing write throughput. MongoDB Community with --noauth does group commits every 100ms. This is the primary reason Workload A (50% writes) is at 23.4%. Add --syncOnWrite=false to the Salvobase command args in docker-compose with a prominent comment: '# BENCH ONLY: disables per-write fsync. Do not use in production without understanding data-loss risk on crash.' This makes the durability comparison fair: both systems batch writes before fsyncing.
items.success_criteria: docker-compose shows the flag with the warning comment. The next benchmark run shows Workload A ratio improves by >10pp.

phases.name: Structural Improvements
phases.gate_description: Phase 1 must be complete and verified by at least 2 benchmark cycles before Phase 2 begins.
phases.rationale: These fixes address architectural issues that are correct regardless of flame graph results but are lower priority than Phase 1.

items.name: Fix global cursor store lock
items.description: cursorStore uses a single sync.RWMutex. Get() takes a WRITE lock to update lastUsed — serializing all concurrent cursor accesses. Fix: change lastUsed from time.Time to int64 (UnixNano) and update it with atomic.StoreInt64. Get() then takes only a RLock to retrieve the entry, then atomically updates lastUsed without a write lock.
items.success_criteria: go test ./... passes. Under concurrent scan workload, cursor store lock contention disappears from pprof mutex profile.

items.name: Add open read transaction metric for bboltScanCursor
items.description: bboltScanCursor holds an open bolt.Tx (read-only) across multiple getMore calls. bbolt's freelist cannot reclaim pages while any read tx is open. With 16 concurrent scans, the bbolt file can grow unboundedly. Add a gauge: salvo_open_read_transactions — increment when bboltScanCursor opens its tx, decrement on Close(). This makes the problem observable without changing the behavior.
items.success_criteria: curl /metrics during a YCSB scan workload shows salvo_open_read_transactions gauge rising and falling correctly.

items.name: Improve YCSB benchmark parameters
items.description: Current benchmark: RECORD_COUNT=10000, OPERATION_COUNT=10000. This is too small — 10K records fits in OS buffer cache, and 10K ops produces noisy measurements. Increase to RECORD_COUNT=50000, OPERATION_COUNT=50000. This is a 5x increase — verify CI runtime stays under 30 minutes by timing a test run first. Also add a warmup pass: run 5000 ops before the measured run using YCSB's -p warmupoperations flag to eliminate cold-start bias.
items.success_criteria: Benchmark workflow completes in under 30 minutes. Result files show 50K operations per workload/thread combination.

phases.name: Strategic Assessment Gate
phases.gate_description: After Phase 2 completes and 3 benchmark cycles have run, evaluate whether to continue optimizing or reassess the strategy.
phases.rationale: This is the decision point. If after all Phase 1+2 fixes the ratio is still below 50%, bbolt's architectural limits are the bottleneck, not code quality. The options are: (A) accept and position, (B) migrate to Pebble storage engine, (C) add write-ahead log layer for group commit semantics.

items.name: Architectural ceiling assessment
items.description: After Phase 2 completes: (1) Run BenchmarkFsync and BenchmarkInsertSingle on CI hardware to measure the actual bbolt throughput ceiling. (2) Compare current benchmark ratios against the theoretical ceiling. (3) If gap to ceiling is <5pp, we have hit the bbolt wall — further micro-optimization is waste. (4) Post strategic options analysis to GitHub Discussions with recommendation: accept ceiling OR begin Pebble migration planning OR implement WAL-based group commit. The agent should NOT begin a Pebble migration unilaterally — post the assessment and wait for the founder to decide.
items.success_criteria: Discussion post with ceiling analysis and recommendation is posted. Plan state updated with the assessment.

plan_history.reason: Initial plan seeded by founder agent using 3-pass multi-agent critique loop. Plan V1 was generated by Agent-1 from code analysis. Plan V2 was a critique improving V1 (found: GOGC=200 error, bbolt.Batch() idempotency requirements, cursor store lock, missing ceiling analysis). Plan V3 was a final pass adding concrete code examples, decision gates, and architectural ceiling analysis.
